reason: The cited evidence does not address oxide layer formation, its effect on surface mobility, or its role in suppressing segregation. E1 shows thermal stability of a different alloy (Ru-5 MEA) without an oxide layer, and E2 reports catalytic performance of PtPdCoCuNi at room temperature without any high-temperature cycling or oxide study. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: A thin surface oxide layer can be engineered on PtPdCoCuNi HEA nanoparticles
This oxide layer acts as a physical/chemical barrier that inhibits surface atom mobility
Inhibited surface mobility suppresses elemental segregation and sintering at high temperatures
Suppressing segregation preserves the single-phase solid solution structure
Preserving the solid solution maintains catalytic and thermoelectric performance
